scope._includedProducts: Used CHPL and product-research materials for CHPL ID 10914 (OfficeEMR), the EHI Export page, and the downloaded export artifacts. Included only the OfficeEMR family because the research and phase-2 evidence explicitly describe the same certified EHR/product surface and one export documentation set. Excluded non-OfficeEMR variants to avoid conflating with separate legacy exports or unrelated products. Certainty high.
scope._excludedProducts: Excluded ENTChoice and other iSALUS offerings because these are referenced as specialty-related offerings, not the OfficeEMR CHPL-certified product line under review. Also excluded InfoDive "Data Export" items because the export docs and sources repeatedly distinguish them as a separate legacy CSV mechanism, not the (b)(10) EHI export. Certainty high.
excludedProducts: Legacy InfoDive data export (separate CSV-based mechanism)
scope._versionsInScope: Included OfficeEMR with current EHI Export artifacts identified in phase-2 (`OfficeEMR_B10_Schema_v1-OCT2023`, `ehi-export-page` artifacts, and sample export `311322`) plus the matching CHPL-certified product period. Excluded other potential future schemas because no evidence was collected for a different versioned schema in scope here. Certainty medium due an explicit "HT1 coming soon" note that suggests pending changes.
versionsInScope: OfficeEMR (CHPL certification context referenced as v2021 / CHPL ID 10914)

scope.scopeNotes: Single product-family abstraction: OfficeEMR EHI (b)(10) export artifacts only.

exportPaths._mechanism: Used the phase-2 report and KnowledgeOwl EHI Export instructions. Explicitly states single-patient export is performed in the app by users with the EHI Export role, generated as a ZIP-like bundle. No API or FHIR endpoint is used for this path. Alternatives (g(10) API paths and legacy InfoDive CSV exports) were rejected because the report marks them as separate systems. Certainty high.
exportPaths._container: Downloaded ZIP sample and single-patient documentation describe all entities as separate JSON files/arrays, implying a bundled multi-file payload per export operation. Certainty high.
exportPaths._formats: Parsed `sample-export` artifacts: each entity is one JSON file; no evidence of FHIR/XML/CSV as primary payload for this path. Certainty high.
exportPaths._standardProfile: No USCDI/FHIR/CCDA profile enforcement is described for the primary export payload; artifacts are vendor-native schemas and data dictionaries. Therefore marked as vendor-native. Certainty high.
exportPaths._selfService: User can trigger and download from the Reports portal with role-based access and immediate ZIP completion status. No queue or vendor handoff is described for this single-patient path. Certainty medium.
exportPaths._operationalBurden: Single patient flow is straightforward (role-enabled UI, request, completion, download). Burden is low-moderate and lower than practice-wide exports. Certainty high.
exportPaths.notes: Requires EHI Export role in UI; appears self-service for in-portal exports.

exportPaths._mechanism: Phase-2 notes for OfficeEMR EHI Export state "all-patient" export is initiated by users with EHI Practice Export role in the same portal, then handled through the iSALUS Data Export team. This is materially different from immediate single-patient flow due human/process dependency. Certainty high.
exportPaths._container: Evidence describes practice-level export as downloadable as export files from the same mechanism; no direct API-based pull path described. Certainty high.
exportPaths._formats: The practice export is described as the same EHI export artifact family, so the same JSON entity-file structure applies. Certainty high.
exportPaths._standardProfile: No standardized API/profiles are identified for the practice-export stream; same vendor-native file set is used. Certainty high.
exportPaths._selfService: Although users can request it, the documentation describes a Data Export team handoff and ~15-day delivery, which means it is not fully self-service without staff/vendor operations. Certainty high.
exportPaths._operationalBurden: Additional role coordination plus manual/assisted fulfillment and long turnaround (about 15 days) creates high operational burden. Certainty high.
exportPaths.notes: Practical for migrations/large extractions, but not immediate and dependent on internal delivery processes.

documentation._hasDataDictionary: The Excel dictionary file (`iSalus_EHI_ExportDataElements_published_version1_Oct2023_pristine.xlsx`) and PDF field pages are explicitly downloaded under phase-2 and list export data dictionaries by entity. Certainty high.
documentation._hasMachineReadableSchema: The `OfficeEMR_B10_Schema_v1-OCT2023` ZIP contains JSON Schema files for each export entity. Certainty high.
documentation._describesFieldNames: The schemas and XLSX include field names for each entity; sample JSON exports show matching keys in practice. Certainty high.
documentation._describesFieldTypes: JSON Schemas define type objects for every exported field. Some nullable fields are not modeled with ideal nullable constructs, but base type information is present. Certainty high.
documentation._describesFieldSemantics: Field semantics are documented in the XLSX and PDF dictionary as plain-English descriptions; this supplements schema typing. Certainty high.
documentation._describesValueSets: No authoritative value sets/enums are documented; schemas use string/object broadly and do not enumerate accepted code sets. Value set references are absent in available artifacts. Certainty high.
documentation._describesRelationships: Evidence shows shared IDs (`patientId`, `claimId`, etc.) and implied links in narrative, but no ER diagram or formal relationship section is provided. Alternatives were rejected because no explicit FK/ER docs are present in artifacts. Certainty medium.
documentation._describesKeysConstraints: Schemas and dictionary describe field-level properties but do not consistently document requiredness, key/cardinality invariants, or constraints beyond type and naming. Therefore conservative marking as partial. Certainty high.
documentation._hasSampleData: A full single-patient sample ZIP (`export-311322-voct2023.zip`) with 58 JSON files was collected; readme links back to format docs. Certainty high.
documentation._sampleRepresentativeness: Sample export is realistic but limited to one patient and does not include every possible entity/file type (e.g., several schema entities absent in sample). So representativeness is moderate. Certainty high.
documentation._docsCurrentness: The evidence includes last-modified and active follow-up content (e.g., HT1 updates, Q1 2026 note). However, there is no explicit changelog in the artifacts themselves. Certainty medium.
documentation._maturity: Given availability of dictionary, machine schema, and sample exports in one place, implementation guidance is workable. Missing value sets/relationship formalism and mixed-format date conventions reduce implementation completeness. Certainty high.
documentation.notes: Strong overall documentation surface; strongest gap is semantic detail beyond simple typing.

fidelityRisk._representationType: The artifacts expose a large set of entity JSON files that map directly to product concepts (appointments, claims, labs, notes, documents, etc.), indicating direct projection of vendor-native model structures rather than a narrow external standard slice. Certainty high.
fidelityRisk._mappingTarget: No evidence of a projection into FHIR/CCDA for this export; the same native JSON model is described end-to-end. Certainty high.
fidelityRisk._projectionLossRisk: Evidence is broad (clinical + claims + communications + specialty entities), and not obviously a pure subset. But absence of explicit telehealth/intake/fax/domain-specific modules raises moderate risk that some EHI-adjacent content is omitted. Certainty high.
fidelityRisk._conflationRisk: Entities are separated by file, and sample data contains dedicated structures for many workflows. Conflation risk is lower than in compact summary APIs, but partially possible when specialty/custom templates collapse into generic encounter structures. Certainty high.
fidelityRisk._reconstructionDifficulty: A third party can likely reconstruct a longitudinal record using patientId links and array entities, but missing explicit constraints and mixed value formats increase integration effort and interpretation effort. Certainty high.
fidelityRisk._keyLossPatterns: No evidence was found for explicit telehealth session records, patient portal activity logs, and fax/transmission workflow artifacts. Value sets are undeclared, and some schema/entity relationships are implicit only; these are likely areas of semantic loss in downstream consumption. Certainty high.

fidelityRisk._likelyOmittedAreas: Given CHPL-wide scope claims, potential omissions are where product marketing mentions modules but export dictionary does not show dedicated files. Missing areas were not inferred broadly; they are limited to weak or unconfirmed evidence only. Certainty medium.

accessConstraints._docsPubliclyAccessible: Direct curl and PDF export access demonstrate public availability without login, CAPTCHA, or API key. The page and files are downloadable from public URLs. Certainty high.
accessConstraints._roleRestricted: EHI export workflow mentions role requirements (`EHI Export`, `EHI Practice Export`) in the UI path. This is an in-product gate but not external authentication, so marked role restricted. Certainty high.
accessConstraints._vendorInvolvementNeeded: Practice-wide export requires Data Export team execution and 15-day fulfillment. Single-patient export is self-serve. Because one supported pathway is vendor-assisted, this flag is set to yes. Certainty high.

overall._posture: Evidence shows extensive native EHI export coverage across core clinical, operational, and billing domains with concrete schema + sample artifacts. However, missing value sets and potential uncovered specialist modules prevent marking this as high-fidelity-complete. Therefore posture is best set to 'usable_but_partial'. Certainty high.
overall._completenessScore: Scored 4 because the export includes both clinical and billing domains broadly, but certain module-adjacent domains are not clearly represented (telehealth/e-fax/intake), and relationship/version semantics are lightly documented. Certainty high.
overall._technicalUsabilityScore: Scored 3 due strong machine-readable artifacts and sample outputs, balanced by missing value-set documentation and implicit relational constraints. Certainty high.
overall._confidence: Moderate-to-high confidence from direct artifacts and structured sample; reduced by the fact that evidence is single-vendor documentation and one sample patient. Certainty high.
overall._strongestSignal: The strongest signal is the complete artifact trio: downloadable JSON schemas, XLSX dictionary, and realistic sample export for the same B10 export version, showing practical implementation intent. Certainty high.
overall.strongestSignal: JSON schema + XLSX dictionary + sample export for the same OfficeEMR B10 package.
overall._biggestRisk: The biggest risk is under-coverage in modules not explicitly represented in export artifacts (notably telehealth and intake/auxiliary workflows) plus weakly documented value semantics and relationships. Certainty high.
overall.biggestRisk: Potential omission of secondary workflow modules and ambiguous field/value semantics.
overall._summary: OfficeEMR shows strong evidence of a broad, vendor-native EHI export implementation covering many EHI domains beyond USCDI, with clear export mechanics and decent self-service usability for single-patient use. Remaining limitations are completeness uncertainty in peripheral modules and downstream interpretability due limited value-set and relational documentation. Certainty high.
overall.summary: OfficeEMR provides a practical, broad non-standard JSON EHI export with significant strengths and some recoverable documentation gaps.

notableFacts: Single-patient EHI export is available as a self-service, immediate portal flow; practice-wide export is assisted and documented at ~15-day turnaround.
EHI export documentation is explicitly not a repackaged g(10) API and uses proprietary JSON entity files rather than FHIR/CCDA.
Export artifacts include 80 JSON Schema files, an Excel data dictionary, and a single-patient sample ZIP.
